answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable kernel of past work instead of a free account: before an agent may trade, it must lock a small stake in a vault that is slashed if it cheats, and its reputation must be earned through attested jobs over time. A newcomer arriving like a boat at a jetty cannot simply clone itself into a hundred identities, because each copy would need its own stake and its own history, so forging an army quickly costs more than gaming one vote or reward.
